cards.title: OpenFOAM versions: cfMesh only in com, surfaceFeatures only in org
cards.when: a meshing route must work beyond OpenFOAM.com; version selection, or an unclear tool error
cards.statement: OpenFOAM versions are not interchangeable in their tools. com (v2412, v2506, v2512, v2606) contains cfMesh (cartesianMesh, pMesh, tetMesh, foamyHexMesh), reconstructParMesh -mergeTol and locationsInMesh (multi-region snappy); org (v14) has no cfMesh, its surfaceFeatureExtract is a stub (rc=0, writes no files), reconstructParMesh has no -mergeTol, locationsInMesh is absent (only the single locationInMesh), but it does have surfaceFeatures + system/surfaceFeaturesDict and foamRun/foamMultiRun. The same STL gives different quality: a 10 mm cube, 16³ cells — com2512/com2606 maxNonOrtho 9.7073°, org14 25.2146° at the same 2584 cells (exp-019).
recipe: installations are declared in sim-project.json → foam.installations {id: {bashrc}}, default selects one
mesh_build / mesh_check / mesh_deliver accept openfoam: "<id>" or an absolute path to etc/bashrc
before running a route it helps to capture the matrix: tools/qa/of_matrix.sh --json --bashrc <bashrc> --out .cache/of-matrix/<id>.json
cfmesh on org: preflight returns route cfmesh needs "cartesianMesh" … pass openfoam:"com2606" or use route snappy/gmsh
org14 + snappy: the scaffold writes system/surfaceFeaturesDict and an explicit file "<name>.stl" in geometry itself; calling surfaceFeatureExtract on org is pointless
org14 + CHT: locationsInMesh is not supported — route D (gmsh OCC) or a per-region run; com remains the primary for multi-region
org-deb unpacked to a non-standard path requires patching FOAM_INST_DIR (it is /opt in the deb)
evidence: exp-019_openfoam-version-matrix: tool matrix and cube E2E on com2512 / com2606 / org14
cfMesh is present only in com; org14: cartesianMesh/pMesh/tetMesh/foamyHexMesh are absent
exp-019: gmshToFoam OK on com2512 and org14; org14 cube delivery via make_delivery — rc=0, round-trip matched
improves: portability of meshing routes between OpenFOAM builds
diagnosing “tool not found” without running the mesher
